artifacts.summary: Design for S2_API_KEY support and an ordered OpenAlex/Crossref fallback chain in literature-discover.sh's Tier 3, preserving the discover-record schema, the four-branch doc_id contract, and the TIER3_STATUS FAILED stderr contract consumed by commands/literature.md.

memory_candidates.content: literature-discover.sh's Tier 3 doc_id derivation has exactly four branches (doi-slug, arxiv_<id>, ss_<paperId>, unknown_<slug>). When adding a new online-discovery provider, never mint a new prefix (e.g. oa_/cr_) — map the provider's own id fields onto the existing four branches (DOI when present, else fall straight to unknown_<slug> if no paperId analog exists), because literature-ingest-online.sh and index-patching downstream key off this exact contract.

literature-discover.sh's TIER3_STATUS: FAILED stderr line is consumed by commands/literature.md via `grep -q 'TIER3_STATUS: FAILED'` plus `grep -o 'http_code=[^ ]*'`. Both are substring/token-tolerant, so a richer multi-provider failure line (extra parenthetical detail after http_code=<token>) is backward compatible as long as the literal FAILED substring and a space-free http_code= token both appear on one line.

As of 2026-09-01, OpenAlex (api.openalex.org) and Crossref (api.crossref.org) both answer anonymous, keyless GET requests successfully (live-verified). A secondary source (Google Groups thread) claims OpenAlex mandated API keys starting Feb 13, but the canonical openalex-docs repo and a live test both contradict that — treat any OpenAlex key requirement as disputed/optional, and design key support as additive (like S2_API_KEY) rather than required.
